title: Ruby and the Wobbly Robot
markdown:
Ruby was amazing at finding shapes. In the Grand Library she could see a triangle in a teacup, a circle in a doorknob, and a square in the neat stacks of books. Her eyes would sparkle, and she’d whisper, “Look, a diamond in that window!”

Dash was always with her. He was a dog whose tail wagged with pure joy. Thump, thump, thump. He understood the importance of a good friend.

Mr. Clive was a clever builder with a beard that tickled like a fluffy cloud and glasses that liked to slide down his nose. He had built a robot named Bob: shiny, silver, friendly blinking lights that winked like curious fireflies. And Bob was ready to do a brand-new dance for everyone!

Ruby bounced. Dash let out a happy little bark, tail already thumping.

“Alright, Bob!” Mr. Clive turned a small dial. “Showtime!”

Bob’s lights blinked green and blue. He started to move. It was not a dance. It was a wobble. One arm twisted. A leg went this way. Not a single smooth move. He spun in a circle that was more of a tumble, and thump! One metal foot landed funny. Then he just stood there, looking wobbly. Grown-ups chuckled, a sound like soft rain. Children giggled, a cascade of happy noises. Bob, the dance robot, was a dance disaster.

“Oh dear,” sighed Mr. Clive. Glasses slid. “It seems Bob has a little wobble in his steps.”

Ruby leaned closer. On a screen on Bob’s chest, bright shapes flashed: a red circle, then a blue square, then a green triangle. But Bob wasn’t making those shapes with his body. He was making wiggly lines.

“Look, Mr. Clive! Bob’s screen shows a circle, but his leg is making a zig-zag!”

Mr. Clive looked at the screen, then at Bob, and rubbed his fuzzy beard. “Ah, I see! You’re right, Ruby. Little mistakes in his dance steps. We call those mistakes bugs. We need to find them and fix them so he can dance right.”

Finding bugs sounded like an interesting adventure to Ruby. Like finding a secret shape. Dash wagged his whole body, a furry blur of happy anticipation.

“How do we fix them?”

“We look for the mistake, the bug, the wobbly bit, and we fix it. Ruby, can you tell me what shape Bob should be making for that first step, the one on his screen?”

Ruby looked at the bright red circle, then at Bob’s zig-zag leg. “He should be kicking his leg in a round shape, like a perfect circle!”

Mr. Clive tapped a small keyboard. Whizz! Bob’s leg moved in a perfect round circle. Dash barked a big sound of approval.

“Wonderful! Now the next shape is a square. What’s Bob doing now?”

Bob was twisting his body like a melted puddle. Ruby pointed. “That’s not a square! A square has four straight sides and four sharp corners!”

Mr. Clive tapped again. Beep! Bob stood up straight, arms at right angles, looking very proud, lights blinking a steady blue.

The screen flashed a green triangle. Bob’s arms went floppy, two noodles with no point at all. Ruby shook her head. “A triangle has three sides that meet in corners. His arms should make a point at the top.”

Mr. Clive tapped a third time. Click! Bob’s arms rose into a neat peak. Dash’s ears pricked. That was the shape.

They kept going. Ruby would see the shape on the screen, then tell Mr. Clive what Bob was actually doing. If Bob was wrong, Mr. Clive fixed the dance steps, and Bob tried again. Metal arms and legs moved with new confidence. Dash’s tail wagged happily when Bob was good, and a little slower when they needed to look closer.

Soon Bob wasn’t wobbling. He was dancing. He twirled and tapped and leaped. Library visitors clapped and cheered. Applause filled the room with warmth. Bob bowed, a graceful move that showed off all his perfect steps. He even did a little shimmy that made everyone laugh with delight.

“You did it!” Ruby bounced on her toes. Dash let out a happy howl everyone understood.

Mr. Clive smiled, ruffling Ruby’s hair. “We did it, thanks to you. A great shape spotter and an even better bug finder. Finding and fixing those little mistakes makes everything work smoothly. You helped Bob dance perfectly.”

His glasses finally rested on the tip of his nose. Bob’s lights winked a calm green. Dash thumped the library carpet. Ruby found one more diamond in the window, just because she could, and Bob, who now knew a circle from a zig-zag and a triangle from two floppy noodles, waited for his next show without a single wobble.
characters: Ruby (shape spotter), Dash (dog), Mr. Clive (builder), Bob (robot)
author: StoryGen Community
